architecture: One agency family (National Rail), one tier-1 hub lock (Carlisle, four/five-line junction, all major operators) with two tier-2 secondary hubs (Oxenholme Lake District — Lakes Line branch point; Barrow-in-Furness — Furness/Cumbrian Coast junction). Penrith is a major WCML station but not a junction, so it is built as a regional station, not a tier-2 hub. Single physical station at every junction — no doNotGroup case anywhere in this catalog (contrast Liverpool City Region's Lime Street/Merseyrail ambiguity or Greater Manchester's Piccadilly/Piccadilly Gardens walk-link). Only 7 of the report's 48 Cumbrian stations are individually named with enough detail to catalog; the remaining 41 are a recorded D2 gap, not invented. See hazard-pack.md and direction-model-memo.md.

Hub lock Carlisle (CAR), secondary hubs Oxenholme Lake District (OXO) and Barrow-in-Furness (BIF). Caledonian Sleeper carries verdict out-reservation and is EXCLUDED from the board at Carlisle, the only Cumbrian station it calls. ARCHITECTURE: one agency family, one tier-1 hub + two tier-2 secondary hubs. See top-level 'architecture' field and direction-model-memo.md for full reasoning.

National Rail modes v1: heavy rail, destination-board model (not line+terminus). BLOCKED pending DARWIN_LDB_TOKEN — see coverageGaps. Build the catalog/adapter normally per Nico's report; do not wire the token until it exists.

Hub lock: Carlisle (CAR CRS), 8 platforms, junction of West Coast Main Line, Settle-Carlisle Line, Tyne Valley Line, Cumbrian Coast Line (four lines directly, a fifth — Lakes Line — reachable via Oxenholme). ~1.97M annual passengers (2017-18 ORR data per report). All operators converge here.

Secondary hubs (tier 2): Oxenholme Lake District (OXO CRS) — WCML/Lakes Line branch point, ~581k passengers; Barrow-in-Furness (BIF CRS) — Furness Line/Cumbrian Coast Line junction, ~652k passengers, 3 platforms.

No doNotGroup case anywhere in this catalog — every junction (Carlisle, Oxenholme, Barrow-in-Furness) is a single physical station per the report, not separate infrastructure or a walk-link pair. See hazard-pack.md H4.

Station count gap: report claims 48 total Cumbrian stations but only individually details 7 (Carlisle, Penrith, Oxenholme, Windermere, Kendal, Barrow-in-Furness, Settle). The report's own aggregate counts for the remainder are internally inconsistent (38 at report line 32 vs. 41 at report line 102) — NOT resolved by this pack. Only the 7 detailed stations are catalogued below; see coverageGaps.

Board eligibility: Northern Trains, TransPennine Express, Avanti West Coast, CrossCountry (if confirmed calling) all verdict 'in' (walk-up boardable, no check-in barrier) per oracle report Board eligibility section. Caledonian Sleeper verdict 'out-reservation' (compulsory berth booking) — EXCLUDED from the board at Carlisle, the only Cumbrian station it calls. Consistent with Rest of Scotland (excluded at Aberdeen/Inverness/Fort William/Mallaig) and Liverpool City Region (excluded, does not call Lime Street) verdicts for the same service — see hazard-pack.md.

Cross-region boundaries checked against already-merged adjacent packs per dispatch instruction: Rest of Scotland's published-network.json does not claim Lockerbie or any station south of its four hubs (Perth/Inverness/Aberdeen/Dundee) — no live overlap with Cumbria's Carlisle-anchored northern boundary. Greater Manchester's published-network.json does not claim Preston, Wigan, or Settle — no live overlap with Cumbria's southern boundary. Both checks confirm, not just assume, the oracle report's own 'no overlap identified' assessment (report line 79). See hazard-pack.md H2/H6.

No 'lines' array is provided for National Rail — no printed route/line map to transcribe, same as every National Rail-only region packed so far. This is a flat station list (one hub, two secondary hubs, four regional/branch stations named individually).

stationGroups.name: Carlisle
stationGroups.class: 8 platforms. Junction of West Coast Main Line (north to Scotland, south to Preston/Manchester), Settle-Carlisle Line (east to Leeds), Tyne Valley Line (east to Newcastle), Cumbrian Coast Line (south/west to Barrow-in-Furness/Workington). Single physical station, all major operators converge. ~1.97M annual passengers (2017-18 ORR data). Report lines 25, 88.

excludedOperators.reason: Compulsory berth/cabin reservation; calls at Carlisle for supply/crew change. Boarding restricted to booked passengers only, staff platform check-in 60-90 min before departure. Report lines 45-47, 50, 66.

stationGroups.name: Oxenholme Lake District
stationGroups.class: West Coast Main Line junction with branch point to Lakes Line (Kendal, Windermere). ~581k annual passengers (2017-18). Report line 27, 51, 91.

stationGroups.name: Barrow-in-Furness
stationGroups.class: 3 platforms. Junction of Furness Line (north to Ulverston, Lancaster direction) and Cumbrian Coast Line (north to Workington, Carlisle). Southern terminus for both lines' Cumbrian extent. ~652k annual passengers (2017-18). Report line 30, 55, 92.

stationGroups.name: Penrith
stationGroups.role: regional major station (not a junction — not promoted to tier-2 hub)
stationGroups.class: West Coast Main Line, ~17 miles south of Carlisle. Regional and intercity services. Report line 26, 52.

regional.name: Windermere
regional.class: Lakes Line branch terminus (Oxenholme -> Kendal -> Windermere). Tourist/commuter hub for Lake District. Report line 28, 53.

regional.name: Kendal
regional.class: Lakes Line, between Oxenholme and Windermere. Lake District market town. Report line 29, 54.

regional.name: Settle
regional.class: Settle-Carlisle Line, ~48 miles south of Carlisle. Southern boundary of Cumbria on this line; route continues south to Hellifield (outside Cumbria scope, toward Lancashire/Greater Manchester). Report line 31, 56, 79.

excludedServices.reason: Compulsory berth/cabin reservation, all passengers must book sleeping accommodation in advance. Calls at Carlisle only within this catalog, for supply/crew change. Report lines 45-47, 50, 66-68.
